newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 25.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Vaclav Havel addressed the German parliament yesterday, ending the Czech side of the Czech-German Declaration. Havel spoke of Europe as a common community.

- One of the 11 people accused of embezzling more than 100 million crowns from Agrobanka is the director of the financial group Motoinvest, Jan Dienstl. At the time of the doubtful transactions, Motoinvest was a significant shareholder of the bank.

- Former Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev will arrive in Prague today for the funeral of Zdenek Mlynar, a former schoolmate and Prague Spring reformer. He will also meet with President Vaclav Havel.

- The state treasury will lose at least 0.5 billion crowns in the liquidation of the indebted railway health insurance company Gral, which will merge with the Interior Ministry's insurance company. This will create the second largest general health insurance company in the country.
- During the first quarter of this year, there were 15,683 new passenger cars sold on the domestic market, a year-on-year increase of nearly 20 percent.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Union Banka will introduce new credits for covering import deposits next week.
- The Czech cabinet is sceptical of a Slovak proposal for dividing former federal property, because the Czech Republic would lose about 21.7 billion crowns with this resolution.

The Dutch company Beheer-En Belegginsmaatschappij Bruwabel and its owner, American National Fuel Gas Company, obtained seven places on the 12 member board of directors of Severoceske Teplarny (SCT) yesterday. Bruwabel recently obtained 35 percent of SCT.
- Skoda Ostrov won the tender to supply 14 buses to Mlada Boleslav. It defeated Mercedes Benz, Volvo Bus Corporation and other world companies.
- The German international concern Eckes will enter the tender for the privatisation of 94 percent of liqueur Becherovka. Plzensky Prazdroj should also enter the tender.
PRAVO - Parliament's expenses will have to be cut by 198 million crowns. The Senate's expenses should be reduced by 117 million and the Supreme Control Administration's by 23.5 million crowns.

- The Industry and Trade Ministry is preparing changes in the list of products which will be burdened with import deposits when they are imported into the Czech Republic. Products such as paints, lacquers and flour will be taken off the list, while other products, such as toys, will be added.
- Ceska Rafinerska had pre-tax profits last year of 1.172 billion crowns, with a total turnover of 36.63 billion crowns.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB) announced on Thursday that it will increase its interest rates on dated accounts for consumer clients by 0.1 percent.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The Senate approved a new customs law and a law for food and tobacco products yesterday in order to strengthen competence among customs officials and move nearer towards the EU.
- Yesterday, the Finance Ministry finished an improved proposal for issuing no-interest 200,000 crown loans for housing. The proposal was sent to the Regional Development Ministry.
- Pope John Paul II will begin an official papal visit to the Czech Republic today. He is expected to arrive in Prague at 18:00 (1600 GMT).
